description: Sotorasib (LUMAKRAS) CodeBreaK 100 Phase 2 trial results — NEJM publication June 2021
source_citation: Skoulidis F et al. NEJM 2021;384:2371-2381. Amgen press release June 1, 2021.
notes: First-in-class KRAS G12C inhibitor. Phase 2 results in NSCLC. ORR 37.1%, DCR 80.6%. Led to accelerated approval May 28, 2021 — NDA was approved before this Phase 2 publication.

raw_document.title: Sotorasib for Lung Cancers with KRAS p.G12C Mutation — CodeBreaK 100 Phase 2 Results
raw_document.raw_text:
BACKGROUND: KRAS p.G12C is the most common KRAS mutation in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Sotorasib is a first-in-class, irreversible, covalent inhibitor of KRAS p.G12C.

METHODS: We conducted a phase 2, single-arm trial (CodeBreaK 100; NCT03600883) of sotorasib 960 mg once daily in patients with KRAS p.G12C-mutated NSCLC who had received at least one prior systemic therapy. The primary end point was objective response rate (ORR).

RESULTS: A total of 124 patients were enrolled. The ORR was 37.1% (95% CI, 28.6 to 46.2), with 4 complete responses and 42 partial responses. The disease control rate (DCR) was 80.6%. The median duration of response was 11.1 months (95% CI, 6.9 to not reached). The median progression-free survival was 6.8 months (95% CI, 5.1 to 8.2), and the median overall survival was 12.5 months (95% CI, 10.0 to not reached).

Safety: Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) of any grade occurred in 69.8% of patients. Grade 3 or 4 TRAEs occurred in 21.0% of patients. The most common TRAEs were diarrhea (31.5%), nausea (19.4%), and elevated alanine aminotransferase (15.3%). No drug-related deaths were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Sotorasib induced durable responses in patients with heavily pretreated KRAS p.G12C-mutated NSCLC. The safety profile was manageable.
